what_it_does: This work addresses a bottleneck in tiny IoT devices powered by solid-state batteries: the battery's internal resistance limits how much peak power can be delivered in short bursts, even though the battery contains plenty of energy. The paper introduces a power-management chip that stores energy in an external capacitor (an electrical storage device like a tiny battery) and uses a switched-capacitor converter—essentially a clever relay circuit that rapidly charges and discharges—to extract and deliver that stored energy at the moment of peak demand. The circuit achieves very high efficiency, delivering 40 times more useful burst energy than prior approaches.
